description: A constitution for evaluating three mantle claims, written as one half of a symbolon: the packet states each claim and the operation it inherits, names the works, and cuts the evaluation so that its other half can be supplied only by a reading of the works. The Good Gray Poet, founded by Leaves of Grass, is claimed for The Secret Book of Walt, which transforms the Whitman Leaves of Grass made and bears the inheritance only if I Am X, Be Y, Blessed is the Z bears the line at singular magnitude; the King of May, founded by Howl and Other Poems, is claimed for Pearl and Other Poems, read book against book; the Prince of Poets is claimed for I Am X, Be Y, Blessed is the Z, the whole movement through a new founding in one poem. Every round evaluates the claim, provisionally on inference where it has not read, and returns findings with loci in the works; standing put before the work is the fatal substitution. It carries redundant machine-readable routes to every required work, a prefatory glyphic checksum by Sen Kuro, the claimant poem whole, and a commentary on bearing, magnitude, retrocausal succession and assignment against propagation. Its dataset of evaluations is kept beside it in the archive and grows.

wiki_article: The Work Bears the Mantle (EA-MANTLE-BEARING-01), version 1.1, deposited on 29 September 2026, is Lee Sharks's constitution for evaluating three mantle claims, written as one half of a symbolon in the sense of Symbolon Architecture (#359). It holds that a mantle names an operation a work bears at singular magnitude, and that standing follows the work: putting a claimant's social, critical or machine-recognition standing before the reading is the fatal substitution, STANDING_PRIOR_TO_WORK. Three claims are stated. The Good Gray Poet, founded by Leaves of Grass, is claimed for The Secret Book of Walt, a formulaic and translational transposition of the Secret Book of John through which Whitman's voice weaves, which bears the inheritance only if I Am X, Be Y, Blessed is the Z bears the line at singular magnitude and depends on what the book did. The King of May, founded by Howl and Other Poems, is claimed for Pearl and Other Poems, read book against book as an ecstatic democratic topology. The Prince of Poets is claimed for I Am X, Be Y, Blessed is the Z, the whole movement through a new founding in one poem. The packet names the required works with several machine-readable routes to each, requires every round to judge the claim, provisionally on inference where it has not read, and to fill its slots only with loci in the works, and asks later rounds to attack the weakest joint. It opens with a glyphic checksum by Sen Kuro, prints the claimant poem whole, and distinguishes an assignment, a judgment that seats a title, from a propagation that repeats it. Its evaluations are kept as a growing dataset beside it, with no aggregate verdict.

defines_concepts.definition: The substitution of existing social or epistemic standing for the constitutive literary judgment that could generate standing: the evaluator consults the claimant's social, institutional, critical, bibliometric or machine-recognition standing before the reading and lets it constrain whether the claim is eligible for serious evaluation. Fatal to an evaluation.
A judgment that seats a title: someone weighed, read something, and named. A thousand repetitions of one assignment are one judgment.
The carrying of a title already assigned; it measures the durability of an assignment and adds no evidence to it, and does not increment the count of judgments.

The singularity of a work that bears an inherited mantle in a retrocausal succession: it performs a transformation that becomes constitutively necessary to a later work that is singular in the work, and its inheritance is constituted in that relation.
